Session-a is a real interactive hermes TUI session (user typed prompts, agent worked — m5/m6 used scripted one-shot children) whose typed mid-session `/ctxvm-handoff /tmp/ctxvm-m7/a 3` pause operated the design §2 chain end-to-end through the systemd service (flush → era copies → export --turn 3 --odps → verified=True), CONTINUED tracing through turn 4 (pause is not teardown), and flushed the full trace at /ctxvm-trace stop + exit. Session-b is a genuinely fresh chat (bare `hermes`, no prior context) booted with CTXVM_RESUME_FROM=<package>: the boot verify chain ran BEFORE any hook work (replay exit 0 at turn 3, projection surfaced, diagnostic diff) and the canonical sidecar gained the resumeFrom evidence object; the resumed agent then rebuilt its knowledge strictly from the package artifacts (llms.txt-led), verified the package itself, found a real mirror regression mid-verify, and produced a handoff report — the product demonstrated on its own capture. The capture path was itself the debugging subject: typed dispatch plus all hooks and turns run INSIDE hermes-gateway.service, whose boot-time env and plugin imports are frozen (TUI shell exports are inert for the service runtime); fixed by `systemctl --user set-environment CTXVM_*…` + service restart. Operator rulings (2026-10-26): hermes both sides, same harness (design §4 does not claim cross-harness handoff — the hermes /ctxvm-handoff handler still lacks the TS adapter's handoff_name=CTXVM_TRACE_NAME pass-through, so the pause needs CTXVM_HANDOFF_NAME equal to the trace flush name; run-1 at 12:21 paused the flushed 'session-a' against the name 'handoff' and exited 2 — archived /tmp/ctxvm-m7/a-run1 — and the 11:38 fail-closed resume boot, before any package existed, is the negative twin of session-b's verified boot); mid-session typed pause at turn 3 with real declared pages.
